question.text: A perfect gas at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is heated at constant pressure so as to double its volume. The final temperature of the gas will be, close to

solution.text:
Given, $V_1=V$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& V_2=2 V \\
& T_1=27^{\circ}+273=300 \mathrm{~K} \\
& T_2=?
\end{aligned}
$$
From charle's law
$$
\frac{V_1}{T_1}=\frac{V_2}{T_2}(\because \text { Pressure is constant })
$$
or, $\frac{V}{300}=\frac{2 V}{T_2}$

$$
\therefore \quad T_2=600 \mathrm{~K}=600-273=327^{\circ} \mathrm{C}
$$
